title: JMAP Chat adopts draft-atwood-jmap-i18n: applicability table, Message language, drop redundant UTF-8 text
description:
Re-scoped 2026-11-15: the generic i18n work (client language preference, generic locale/localizations, encoding, normalization, collation, lengths/truncation, names-are-display-text, PRECIS, time zones, bidi/confusables, server-written text) moved to jmap-chat-spec-dhv2, draft-atwood-jmap-i18n-00. This bead is now: JMAP Chat adopts that draft. Blocked on dhv2.

Origin: found 2026-11-14 while wiring mimid's JMAP Chat.name to MIMI room metadata (mimid bead mimid-1wgh.51), after a sweep of the MIMI drafts for English text that reaches users (IETF notes/2026-11-14-mimi-issues-from-table-draft.md, item 8). draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 says nothing about language anywhere.

Chat-specific work:

1. Applicability table for draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 (which properties take locale/localizations):
   - Chat: name (L599), description (L602), topic (L623, server-set: server-written text rules apply)
   - ChatContact: displayName (L525), statusText (L540)
   - PresenceStatus: statusText (L1029)
   - Space: name (L881), description (L884); Category: name (L847); SpaceRole: name (L799)
   - Endpoint and MessageAction label (L403, L426)
   - CustomEmoji: name (L931) is an ASCII shortcode identifier, not display text; say that is deliberate and that it is not localized.

2. Message gains an optional 'language' (BCP 47) for the body, filled from mimi-content's per-part language by MIMI gateways (mimi-content-10). The rich body's 'codeblock' lang (L1571) is a syntax hint, not the text's language; say so.

3. Remove the per-property "MUST be valid UTF-8" restatements (login L523, body L706, subject L742, input validation L1755/L1763) and cite I-JSON per dhv2. Keep the real distinction: a plaintext body is text; a ciphertext body is base64url and is never normalized or inspected.

4. Reaction emoji (L486): say how variation selectors (U+FE0F) and skin-tone sequences compare, or two clients' identical reactions don't aggregate. Chat-specific; dhv2 only says keys compare as exact code-point sequences.

5. Name sorts (Space/query L1402, L1495; ChatContact by login L1075) cite Comparator.collation per dhv2. Names-are-display-text (no matching on English role or space names) cites dhv2; same rule as proposed for MIMI room-policy. SpaceRole meaning lives in permissions and position, not name.

6. Truncation points in Chat: lastMessage snippets, notification text, push payloads; cite dhv2's grapheme rule.

7. Companion drafts (mimi-00, federation-00, filenode-00, calendars-00, tasks-00, push-00, wss-00): same applicability pass. Federation carries language/localizations between servers unchanged; push payloads hit the truncation and bidi points.

Unblocks mimid-1wgh.51, which should implement whatever dhv2 and this settle rather than inventing an Accept-Language rule.
